thread:
Mira Joshi: heads-up - client 'Vera Labs' private install reported a brief outage where keystore decrypts returned 403s and our SIEM shows a gap in RBAC audit events. This one looks differentnot just key propagation.
Liam O'Connor: timeline? did any maintenance run?
Mira Joshi: no scheduled rotate. We did push a netpol tighten and an audit-forwarder config change at ~09:12 UTC. First decrypt 403s at 09:14.
sec-bot: Alert: decrypt_403 spike tenant=vera at 2026-04-01T09:14:03Z. Audit gap detected for RBAC_CHANGE events between 09:12 and 09:40. Tag=AUDIT_EGRESS_MISS_178123.
Oncall Ops: paste sanitized keystore-proxy logs?
Mira Joshi: logs:
```
2026-04-01T09:14:02Z keystore-proxy ERROR tenant=vera msg="decrypt denied" code=403 principal=svc-vera-ks key=kms://vera/key-v5
2026-04-01T09:14:03Z hsm-connector WARN principal_lookup failed: principal not found in key policy
2026-04-01T09:14:05Z audit-forwarder ERROR outbound=siem status=502 reason="connection refused"
```
Eli Brown: interesting. So keystore denied due to missing principal binding and simultaneously our forwarder couldn't reach SIEM. Where are audit entries persisted locally?
Oncall Ops: both infra-agent and keystore write local audit to /var/log/keystore/audit.log and /var/log/infra/audit.log. Forwarder tried to send and was refused because netpol egress was tightened (deny-by-default) and the SIEM whitelist was accidentally omitted in the new policy. Netflow shows blocked egress to SIEM IPs 09:12-09:38.
Liam O'Connor: why did principals go missing then? No rotation. Could an emergency RBAC grant have been applied while forwarder was blocked, causing that grant to not appear in SIEM?
Mira Joshi: yes we did an emergency grant at 09:16 to restore service after initial 403s. Command: `kmsctl grant --key key-v5 --principal svc-vera-ks --actions decrypt` executed by oncall. That RBAC_CHANGE didn't arrive in SIEM until 09:39 when we re-opened egress.
sec-bot: Retrieved local audit snippet: `2026-04-01T09:16:12Z audit RBAC_CHANGE actor=oncall@infra principal=svc-vera-ks key=key-v5 reason=emergency-recovery`. Forwarder backlog recorded 84 events.
Eli Brown: this creates two compliance problems: 1) missing immediate audit evidence for the grant window, 2) potential for elevated privilege window if revoke was delayed. Was the grant revoked?
Oncall Ops: we revoked at 09:52 after full investigation. Revoke command: `kmsctl revoke --key key-v5 --principal svc-vera-ks`. SIEM shows both grant and revoke at 09:39 and 09:53 respectively (ingest times).
Liam O'Connor: mitigation path: short-term - provide signed attestation bundle with local audit logs + forwarder ingest timestamps and netflow captures. Long-term - require immutable pre-commit of RBAC changes to on-disk append-only store that is replicated off-cluster before operation completes.
Mira Joshi: Agreed. Also we saw a secondary issue during the incident: a token replay test by Vera's devs showed that an old ephemeral token could be used to hit another pod for ~30s due to kube-proxy conntrack and the proxy's cache allowing the token until TTL expiry. That could have allowed lateral decrypt requests during an emergency grant.
sec-bot: Detected: TOKEN_REPLAY pattern during incident window - same token used from two distinct pod IPs at 09:15:12Z and 09:15:30Z. Recorded as potential replay.
Eli Brown: that's concerning. Attack chain: emergency grant applied while token reuse allowed on another pod could have resulted in cross-pod decrypt during the window. We need three mitigations: cache invalidation on token rotation, reduce proxy token cache TTL floor, and conntrack cleanup on token rotation events.
Oncall Ops: Immediate mitigations we applied for Vera: 1) set environment var TOKEN_CACHE_SAFE_TTL=3s for keystore-proxy, 2) bounced kube-proxy to clear conntrack entries (immediate), 3) reissued ephemeral tokens for service accounts. Customer confirmed no suspicious decrypts in audit.
Liam O'Connor: longer-term actions: 1) implement immutable pre-commit audit store (INF-10101), 2) require audit-forwarder egress exception in netpols during any maintenance or while RBAC_CHANGE backlog > 0 (INF-10102), 3) add automatic local-signed audit bundle upload to S3-like immutable bucket before accepting an emergency RBAC grant (INF-10103), 4) implement auto-revoke TTL for emergency grants with mandatory justification, 5) keystore-proxy hotfix to subscribe to token-rotation events and invalidate caches on rotation (INF-10104), 6) add conntrack cleanup hook to infra-agent when rotating tokens/keys (INF-10105).
Mira Joshi: plus policy: no simultaneous netpol egress hardening and RBAC/key changes in the same maintenance window. Serialize those ops. Add a preflight that asserts SIEM egress is allowed before any RBAC emergency action.
sec-bot: Added incident tags: AUDIT-ECT-178123, TOKEN-REPLAY-178123. Attached artifacts: local audit logs, netflow capture, forwarder backlog dump, token use logs, manual grant/revoke commands.
Eli Brown: compliance note: prepare signed attestation for Vera that contains the precise timeline, hash-signed local audit bundle, SIEM ingest receipts, and confirmation that emergency grant was limited and auto-revoked. Offer to run a joint evidence review.
Oncall Ops: I'll bundle artifacts and produce a signed tarball (ETA 2 hours). Also will start INF-10101-10105 and assign owners.
Liam O'Connor: add alerting: if audit-forwarder backlog > 10 events -> page infra and auto-open egress for 30m. If token used from >1 pod IP within TTL -> mark token as suspected replay and rotate immediately.
Mira Joshi: good. I'll draft the customer comms and postmortem; include remediation, timeline, and our plan to harden private deploy preflight checks. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
